name: Abigail
charge: Upon me, my lord, upon me let this iniquity be: keeping David from shedding blood and avenging himself with his own hand
summary: A woman of good understanding attached to a son of Belial. When she heard that David was coming with four hundred swords for her husband’s railing, she made haste with two hundred loaves, two bottles of wine, five sheep ready dressed, parched corn, raisins and figs, and went down to meet him without telling her lord. She fell at his feet, took the iniquity upon herself, named her husband’s folly without defending it, and told the coming king what the Lord would do for him. David blessed her advice; about ten days later the Lord smote Nabal, and David sent for her.
offenseFull: One of the young men told Abigail what Nabal had done and what David’s men had been to the shepherds, a wall to them both by night and by day, and that evil was determined against their master and all his household. She made haste and took two hundred loaves, two bottles of wine, five sheep ready dressed, five measures of parched corn, a hundred clusters of raisins and two hundred cakes of figs, laid them on asses, and sent her servants on before her; but she told not her husband Nabal (1 Samuel 25:14-19). When she saw David she hasted, lighted off the ass, fell before him on her face and bowed to the ground, fell at his feet, and said, upon me, my lord, upon me let this iniquity be. She was not the one who did anything wrong, and she took that iniquity on herself; she was being the pillar of her house, using wisdom to protect it. She did not turn her lord over to be destroyed, as some women today would be ready to do, and she did not defend him either: let not my lord regard this man of Belial, she said, for as his name is, so is he; Nabal is his name, and folly is with him (1 Samuel 25:23-31). Belial means a child of Satan; she said openly that her husband was the devil the Bible speaks of, and she asked pardon for a trespass that was not hers. Then she told the coming king who he was: the Lord had withheld him from coming to shed blood and from avenging himself with his own hand; the Lord would certainly make her lord a sure house, because he fought the battles of the Lord; his soul would be bound in the bundle of life with the Lord his God, and the souls of his enemies would be slung out as out of the middle of a sling; and when the Lord had appointed him ruler over Israel it would be no grief nor offence of heart to him that he had shed blood causeless or avenged himself. This is a woman who knows what to say, when to say it, and how to say it.
judgmentFull: David said, blessed be the Lord God of Israel, which sent her that day to meet him, and blessed be her advice, and blessed be she, which had kept him that day from coming to shed blood and from avenging himself with his own hand. He received of her hand what she had brought, and told her to go up in peace to her house, for he had hearkened to her voice and accepted her person (1 Samuel 25:32-35). The Lord put the spirit on her, she spoke eloquently, and the king changed his mind. That is the lesson for wives: be in subjection to your own husbands, so that if any obey not the word they may without the word be won by the conversation of the wives, beholding a chaste conversation coupled with fear (1 Peter 3:1). Her chaste conversation was her behaviour, not her mouth; when she heard that David was coming she made that feast and carried it down herself. And the scripture that tells servants to be subject not only to the good and gentle but also to the froward covers the house she was in: enduring grief wrongfully for conscience toward God is thankworthy (1 Peter 2:18-19).

At home she governed the moment of speaking too. Nabal held a feast like the feast of a king and was very drunken, so she told him nothing until the morning light; when the wine was gone out of him and she told him, his heart died within him and he became as a stone, and about ten days after the Lord smote him, that he died. When David heard it he sent and communed with Abigail to take her to him to wife, and she

bowed herself on her face to the earth and said that her handmaid would be a servant to wash the feet of the servants of her lord; then she arose and hasted and rode on an ass with five damsels of hers after her, and went after the messengers of David and became his wife (1 Samuel 25:36-42). That is a very humble act, and even attached to a wicked man she was still in a humble place. She was probably very glad to go, relieved of a man who would not listen, would not take advice, and could not be spoken to. Her household was spared the slaughter, and Nabal’s own judgment was left with the Lord.

taught.title: 1 Samuel 25: Nabal's Folly and Abigail's Wisdom

text.text: But one of the young men told Abigail, Nabal’s wife, saying, Behold, David sent messengers out of the wilderness to salute our master; and he railed on them.
But the men were very good unto us, and we were not hurt, neither missed we any thing, as long as we were conversant with them, when we were in the fields:
They were a wall unto us both by night and day, all the while we were with them keeping the sheep.
Now therefore know and consider what thou wilt do; for evil is determined against our master, and against all his household: for he is such a son of Belial, that a man cannot speak to him.

Then Abigail made haste, and took two hundred loaves, and two bottles of wine, and five sheep ready dressed, and five measures of parched corn, and an hundred clusters of raisins, and two hundred cakes of figs, and laid them on asses.
And she said unto her servants, Go on before me; behold, I come after you. But she told not her husband Nabal.
And when Abigail saw David, she hasted, and lighted off the ass, and fell before David on her face, and bowed herself to the ground,
And fell at his feet, and said, Upon me, my lord, upon me let this iniquity be: and let thine handmaid, I pray thee, speak in thine audience, and hear the words of thine handmaid.

Let not my lord, I pray thee, regard this man of Belial, even Nabal: for as his name is, so is he; Nabal is his name, and folly is with him: but I thine handmaid saw not the young men of my lord, whom thou didst send.

Now therefore, my lord, as the Lord liveth, and as thy soul liveth, seeing the Lord hath withholden thee from coming to shed blood, and from avenging thyself with thine own hand, now let thine enemies, and they that seek evil to my lord, be as Nabal.
And now this blessing which thine handmaid hath brought unto my lord, let it even be given unto the young men that follow my lord.

I pray thee, forgive the trespass of thine handmaid: for the Lord will certainly make my lord a sure house; because my lord fighteth the battles of the Lord, and evil hath not been found in thee all thy days.

Yet a man is risen to pursue thee, and to seek thy soul: but the soul of my lord shall be bound in the bundle of life with the Lord thy God; and the souls of thine enemies, them shall he sling out, as out of the middle of a sling.
And it shall come to pass, when the Lord shall have done to my lord according to all the good that he hath spoken concerning thee, and shall have appointed thee ruler over Israel;

That this shall be no grief unto thee, nor offence of heart unto my lord, either that thou hast shed blood causeless, or that my lord hath avenged himself: but when the Lord shall have dealt well with my lord, then remember thine handmaid.
And David said to Abigail, Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, which sent thee this day to meet me:
And blessed be thy advice, and blessed be thou, which hast kept me this day from coming to shed blood, and from avenging myself with mine own hand.

For in very deed, as the Lord God of Israel liveth, which hath kept me back from hurting thee, except thou hadst hasted and come to meet me, surely there had not been left unto Nabal by the morning light any that pisseth against the wall.
So David received of her hand that which she had brought him, and said unto her, Go up in peace to thine house; see, I have hearkened to thy voice, and have accepted thy person.
Likewise, ye wives, be in subjection to your own husbands; that, if any obey not the word, they also may without the word be won by the conversation of the wives;
Servants, be subject to your masters with all fear; not only to the good and gentle, but also to the froward.
For this is thankworthy, if a man for conscience toward God endure grief, suffering wrongfully.

And Abigail came to Nabal; and, behold, he held a feast in his house, like the feast of a king; and Nabal’s heart was merry within him, for he was very drunken: wherefore she told him nothing, less or more, until the morning light.
But it came to pass in the morning, when the wine was gone out of Nabal, and his wife had told him these things, that his heart died within him, and he became as a stone.
And it came to pass about ten days after, that the Lord smote Nabal, that he died.

And when David heard that Nabal was dead, he said, Blessed be the Lord, that hath pleaded the cause of my reproach from the hand of Nabal, and hath kept his servant from evil: for the Lord hath returned the wickedness of Nabal upon his own head. And David sent and communed with Abigail, to take her to him to wife.
And when the servants of David were come to Abigail to Carmel, they spake unto her, saying, David sent us unto thee, to take thee to him to wife.
And she arose, and bowed herself on her face to the earth, and said, Behold, let thine handmaid be a servant to wash the feet of the servants of my lord.
And Abigail hasted, and arose, and rode upon an ass, with five damsels of hers that went after her; and she went after the messengers of David, and became his wife.
